🏳️‍🌈Regnbue Maraton Film #7🏳️‍🌈 Fuck hvor snakker Nicole Kidman langsomt. Virkelig mange unødvendigt lange scener. Da han skulle købe et kostume, for eksempel. Synes det var en mærkelig og unaturlig diskussion de havde i starten hvor hun ender med at fortælle ham om den fantasi hun havde med naval-officeren. Hvad fanden var der interessant ved den? Jeg fatter virkelig ikke kærligheden folk har for den her. Tror godt jeg forstår det meste af pointen. Han bliver usikker over hendes fantasi, han bliver jalous og vil have sin egen sexuelle oplevelse. Han prøver at være utro men kan aldrig rigtig helt og han finder ud af at han ingen kontrol har, gennem den her kult. Og så finder han tilbage til konen og ender med at værdsætte deres forhold. Det er alt sammen fint nok, men det var bare så kedeligt og uinteressant et plot. Kidman nævner drømme til sidst, der bliver sagt det der med en fake charade til sidst. Så hele eller noget af filmen er fake eller en drøm. Det gør mig endnu mindre interesseret i den. Sværger folk vil bare glaze alt hvad Kubrick laver, lige meget hvad.

The fact that is film has not garnered more attention in a post Epstein era is more terrifying than the film itself. Kubrick created a fantasy of our own reality, to portray such intense dynamics of power and control, the cult orgy scene was not at all remotely related to sex, it was a portrayal of vulnerability, exclusivity, and the allure/primal want. Nicole Kidman character acted more like the villain than the man in the red robes, her final line being “fuck” in relation to all they can do now is “fuck” is the perfect verbalization of that dystopian and disturbing objectification of all parties in the film. The symmetry between the cult scene and kidmans dream was truly beautiful because it portrayed Cruise as being and feeling terrified, powerless and objectified yet deeply pleasured while Kidmans was the same. It is a shame this was Kubrick’s last film, but it was a great one, and a disturbing one.

Why was this highkey a Christmas movie I didn’t dislike this movie at all actually contrary to my rating. I really loved that this touched on the topic of is it as bad to just think about cheating as it is to actually do it and I loved how the cult represented that as well. I actually really liked Tom Cruise’s performance in this too being it’s actually my first movie of his (I know shocker) and I loved how a lot of the scenes with Bill and Alice were long talking scenes. I was never bored during this movie. Now with saying all that my biggest problem is that I just wanted more from every aspect of this movie. Yes the cult was creepy with the masks and oh my gosh was the music creepy during those scenes along with the scene of Bill being followed but from both of those scenes I just wanted more. I heard from people that this movie was one of the most creepy movies people have ever scene and while the cult scene was unsettling the only thing I found creepy was the music. Then it only lasted for like 20 ish minutes and yes it weaved into the rest of the story after that but I wish there was more to it in the beginning half of the movie vs just the back half of the movie cause while I understand why that scene was there I kinda felt like it was smacked in there as to like oh now this is happening we see the password on the napkin and we gotta find out what it is but it’s not a build up to it. Now the scene of Bill being followed was good but I wanted so much more from it. I wanted him to be followed longer and lowkey I wish he was chased too (I know you aren’t supposed to rate movies based off of what you would do). I just wanted so much more from that whole scene. Lastly, I did feel like the 2 hours and 30 ish minutes went by really fast. I didn’t find myself wanting it to end or feeling the runtime the whole time it was just that I wanted so much more. Also the random plot of him being a doctor I was just like okay I know that’s not what the movies about at all but that’s just there to be there again with everything feeling like it needed to be more. I really wish I loved this more because I’ve seen so many great reviews and it’s even a couple of peoples favorite movies. Maybe this is one I’ll try to watch again in the future.

While cinematography-wise beautifully done, I thought it was a little odd seeing Tom Cruise in a role like this when I’m so used to seeing him as Ethan, Reacher, or Maverick. But honestly, he gave a great performance. I also really enjoyed Nicole Kidmans acting. The movie itself was a slow burner, and the story felt like it was constantly torn between marriage issues, trust issues, and this higher-power society. I do feel like the ending was a bit of a letdown. It almost felt like the movie suddenly hit a wall and just stopped. Still, it was a rather good film, and I can definitely see why it became a cult classic.

Visuals carry this thing hard, every frame drenched in that blue light, genuinely gorgeous stuff, Kubrick clearly cared more about mood than moving the plot along. But man, the pacing's backwards Too much time wandering NYC at night, not enough time actually sitting inside the sex cult, which gets like one scene and then Ziegler hand-waves the whole thing away the next morning. Felt like wasted potential, the concept deserved more room to breathe than the "will he/won't he cheat" stuff did. Ending's not bad, works as two people mutually agreeing to stop pulling a thread neither wants unraveled, but the movie around it is just kind of meh.
